        "contents": "# Codex v1.2.0 セマンティックバージョンアップグレード実装ログ\n\n**実装日**: 2025-11-03  \n**バージョン**: v1.2.0  \n**実装者**: zapabob\n\n---\n\n## 📋 概要\n\nCodex Tauri GUIアプリケーションのセマンティックバージョンをv1.1.0からv1.2.0にアップグレード。Quest 2/Virtual Desktop対応、VR/AR機能強化を含む重要なリリース。\n\n---\n\n## 🎯 実装内容\n\n### 1. バージョン番号更新\n\n#### 更新ファイル\n\n**&#96;codex-rs/tauri-gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml&#96;**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[package]\nversion = \"1.2.0\"  # v1.1.0 → v1.2.0\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**&#96;codex-rs/tauri-gui/package.json&#96;**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"name\": \"codex-tauri\",\n  \"version\": \"1.2.0\"  // v1.1.0 → v1.2.0\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**&#96;codex-rs/tauri-gui/src/App.tsx&#96;**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n&lt;p className=\"version\"&gt;v1.2.0&lt;/p&gt;  // UI表示も更新\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. 主要な変更点（v1.1.0 → v1.2.0）\n\n#### 🥽 VR/AR機能強化\n\n- **Quest 2最適化**\n  - &#96;Quest2Optimization.tsx&#96;コンポーネント追加\n  - 90Hzリフレッシュレート対応\n  - シャドウマッピング無効化（パフォーマンス向上）\n  - LOD（Level of Detail）実装準備\n\n- **Virtual Desktop対応**\n  - &#96;VirtualDesktopOptimizer&#96;クラス実装\n  - バンド幅最適化アルゴリズム\n  - 動的ビットレート調整\n  - 予測的トラッキング補償\n\n- **VR設定ページ追加**\n  - &#96;VRSettings.tsx&#96; - VRデバイス選択UI\n  - リフレッシュレート設定（72/90/120/144 Hz）\n  - Virtual Desktop最適化トグル\n  - パフォーマンスTips表示\n\n#### 📊 4D Git可視化強化\n\n- **時系列4次元可視化**\n  - &#96;Scene4D.tsx&#96; - 4D空間でのコミットノード配置\n  - 時間軸（W軸）スライダー実装\n  - ハンドトラッキング対応\n  - 空間音響統合準備\n\n#### 🔧 ビルドシステム改善\n\n- **差分ビルドスクリプト**\n  - &#96;watch-build-install.ps1&#96; - ビルド監視＆自動インストール",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "contents": "#### 1. サブエージェントシステム ✨\n- 8種類の専門エージェント\n- 並列実行機能 (&#96;delegate-parallel&#96;)\n- カスタムエージェント作成 (&#96;agent-create&#96;)\n- **影響**: 大（新しいワークフロー提供）\n\n#### 2. 自動オーケストレーション 🤖\n- TaskAnalyzer（複雑度自動判定）\n- AutoOrchestrator（自律並列実行）\n- CollaborationStore（エージェント間通信）\n- **影響**: 大（ClaudeCode超える自動化）\n\n#### 3. ThreeWayMerge実装 🔀\n- FileEditTracker（編集キュー管理）\n- ConflictResolver（自動競合解決）\n- 3つのマージ戦略\n- **影響**: 中（並行編集の安全性向上）\n\n#### 4. Deep Research拡張 🔍\n- 多段探索エンジン（depth 1-5）\n- 引用必須レポート\n- 矛盾検出機能\n- **影響**: 大（新しいリサーチワークフロー）\n\n#### 5. Webhook統合 🔗\n- GitHub API連携\n- Slack通知\n- Custom webhook\n- **影響**: 中（CI/CD統合強化）\n\n#### 6.         "contents": "- Extended by [@zapabob](https://github.com/zapabob)\n- Inspired by Kamui4D project\n\n---\n\n&lt;a name=\"japanese\"&gt;&lt;/a&gt;\n## 📖 日本語\n\n### 🎉 v2.0.0 \"Quantum Leap\" の新機能\n\n**リリース日**: 2025年11月6日  \n**マイルストーン**: カーネル統合型AI-Native OS\n\n#### 🌟 革命的機能\n\n**🎯 プランモード (Blueprint→Plan移行完了)**\n- CLIコマンド: &#96;codex plan&#96; (create, list, execute, approve)\n- 実行戦略: 単一/中央集権型/コンペ型\n- 予算管理とコスト推定\n- 状態永続化とレジューム機能\n\n**🌌 4次元Git可視化 (xyz+時刻軸)** - Kamui4D超え\n- TUI: 3D ASCII可視化＋時刻軸\n- GUI (Tauri): Three.jsインタラクティブ3D\n- CUDA加速: 100,000+コミットを0.05秒で解析\n- リアルタイム再生（タイムラインスライダー）\n- ヒートマップ可視化（コミット頻度）\n- 依存関係グラフ（ノードクラスタリング）\n\n**🥽 VR/AR対応** - 没入型コード探索\n- **Meta Quest 2**: WebXR、コントローラー最適化、90Hz\n- **Meta Quest 3**: ハンドトラッキング、カラーパススルー\n- **Meta Quest Pro**: アイトラッキング、フェイストラッキング\n- **Apple Vision Pro**: visionOS、RealityKit、空間コンピューティング\n- **SteamVR**: Virtual Desktop統合\n\n**🔧 OSカーネル統合** - 深いシステム統合\n- Linuxカーネルモジュール: AIスケジューラー、AIメモリ、AI GPU\n- Windowsカーネルドライバー: WDM/KMDF、ETWトレーシング\n- eBPFモニタリング: リアルタイム性能メトリクス\n- GPU DMA直接制御\n\n**⚡ CUDAランタイム** - あらゆる場面でGPU加速\n- Git解析: 100倍高速化\n- 3D描画: リアルタイム60fps\n- LLM推論: (v2.1.0で実装予定)\n- マルチGPU: (ロードマップ)\n\n**🤖 強化されたサブエージェントシステム** - 8種類以上の専門エージェント\n- 並列実行: 2.6倍高速化\n- コラボレーションストア: エージェント間通信\n- コンフリクト解決: 3種類のマージ戦略",

        "contents": "実装ログ: _docs/2025-10-28_upstream統合とv0.51.0リリース.md\n\n#LLMOps #Rust #AI #MachineLearning #DevOps #OpenAI #Codex #MCP\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n### 英語版\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n🚀 OpenAI Codex v0.51.0 Integration + Custom AI Features Release\n\nDear LLMOps and AI Engineers,\n\nI'm excited to announce the release of Codex v0.51.0-zapabob.1, successfully integrating OpenAI's official repository updates while preserving and enhancing custom AI orchestration features.\n\n## Key Achievements\n\n### 🔄 OpenAI Official Integration\n- Fully merged upstream/main (commit 4a42c4e1)\n- Resolved 9 merge conflicts manually\n- Integrated auth system enhancements (Keyring support)\n- Maintained semantic versioning consistency\n\n### ✨ Custom Features Preserved\n1. **Multi-Agent System**\n   - 8 specialized agents (code-reviewer, sec-audit, test-gen, etc.)\n   - 3x faster processing via parallel execution\n   - Automatic task distribution mechanism\n\n2. **Deep Research Capability**\n   - Google Gemini Search Grounding integration (NEW!)\n   - Multi-backend support (Gemini/DuckDuckGo/Google/Bing)\n   - Contradiction detection &amp; confidence scoring\n   - Citation-backed report generation\n\n3. **MCP Integration**\n   - 15 MCP servers fully operational\n   - Complete Cursor IDE/VSCode compatibility\n   - Serena (21 tools), Playwright, Gemini integration\n\n### 🛠️ Technical Challenges &amp; Solutions\n\n**Major Merge Challenges**:\n1. Rust 2024 edition syntax compatibility → Migrated to nested if statements\n2. EventMsg enum extension (SubAgent events) → Ensured exhaustive pattern matching\n3. AuthManager API changes → Added auth_credentials_store_mode parameter across 3 locations\n4. ratatui_macros dependency removal → Migrated to ratatui::prelude\n\n**Build Statistics**:\n- Incremental build time: 22 minutes (LTO enabled, fully optimized)\n- Clean build: Post 19.2GB cleanup\n- Unified versioning across all 45 workspace members\n\n## Tech Stack\n\n- **Language**: Rust (edition 2021/2024)\n- **Architecture**: Multi-agent orchestration + MCP integration\n- **CI/CD**: Incremental builds with sccache",

        "contents": "//! Dynamic resource management for parallel AI agent execution\n//!\n//! Manages system resources (CPU, memory) and controls concurrent execution\n//! to prevent system overload while maximizing throughput.\n\nuse anyhow::Context;\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse serde::Deserialize;\nuse serde::Serialize;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse sysinfo::CpuRefreshKind;\nuse sysinfo::MemoryRefreshKind;\nuse sysinfo::RefreshKind;\nuse sysinfo::System;\nuse tokio::sync::RwLock;\nuse tokio::sync::Semaphore;\nuse tracing::debug;\nuse tracing::info;\nuse tracing::warn;\n\n/// Resource capacity information\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ResourceCapacity {\n    /// Maximum concurrent tasks allowed\n    pub max_concurrent: usize,\n    /// Currently active tasks\n    pub active_tasks: usize,\n    /// Available slots for new tasks\n    pub available_slots: usize,\n}\n\n/// System resource statistics\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct SystemStats {\n    /// CPU usage percentage (0-100)\n    pub cpu_usage_percent: f32,\n    /// Memory used in bytes\n    pub memory_used_bytes: u64,\n    /// Total memory in bytes\n    pub memory_total_bytes: u64,\n    /// Memory usage percentage (0-100)\n    pub memory_usage_percent: f32,\n    /// Number of active agent tasks\n    pub active_agents: usize,\n    /// Number of CPU cores\n    pub cpu_cores: usize,\n}\n\n/// RAII guard for resource slots\n/// Automatically releases slot when dropped\npub struct ResourceGuard {\n    _permit: tokio::sync::SemaphorePermit&lt;'static&gt;,\n    active_tasks: Arc&lt;RwLock&lt;usize&gt;&gt;,\n}\n\nimpl Drop for ResourceGuard {\n    fn drop(&amp;mut self) {\n        // Note: We can't await in Drop, so we spawn a task\n        let active_tasks = Arc::clone(&amp;self.active_tasks);\n        tokio::spawn(async move {\n            let mut tasks = active_tasks.write().await;\n            if *tasks &gt; 0 {\n                *tasks -= 1;\n            }\n        });\n    }\n}\n\n/// Manages dynamic resource allocation for agent orchestration\npub struct ResourceManager {\n    /// Maximum concurrent tasks (CPU cores * 2)",

        "contents": "# Codex Architecture\n\nComplete architecture documentation for the Codex AI-Native OS project.\n\n## 📐 High-Level Architecture\n\n![Architecture Diagram](docs/architecture/codex-architecture.svg)\n\n## 🏗️ System Layers\n\n### Layer 1: Hardware\n\n- **CPU**: x86_64/ARM64, 16+ cores\n- **GPU**: NVIDIA (CUDA 12), AMD (ROCm), Intel (oneAPI)\n- **Memory**: DDR4/DDR5, 64GB+, NUMA-aware\n- **Storage**: NVMe SSD, PCIe 4.0\n\n### Layer 2: Kernel Space\n\n#### Linux Kernel Modules\n\n**AI Scheduler** (&#96;ai_scheduler.ko&#96;):\n- GPU-aware process scheduling\n- Priority boost for AI tasks\n- Real-time latency optimization\n- &#96;/proc/ai_scheduler&#96; interface\n\n**AI Memory** (&#96;ai_mem.ko&#96;):\n- 256MB pinned memory pool\n- 4KB block allocation\n- Zero-copy GPU transfers\n- &#96;/proc/ai_memory&#96; statistics\n\n**AI GPU** (&#96;ai_gpu.ko&#96;):\n- Direct GPU DMA control\n- PCI device management\n- Kernel-space GPU launches\n- &#96;/proc/ai_gpu&#96; monitoring\n\n#### Windows Kernel Driver\n\n**AI Driver** (&#96;ai_driver.sys&#96;):\n- WDM/KMDF filter driver\n- Thread priority boost\n- Non-paged memory pool\n- ETW performance tracing\n\n#### eBPF Tracing\n\n- GPU utilization monitoring\n- Inference latency histogram\n- Real-time performance metrics\n- BCC/bpftrace integration\n\n### Layer 3: User Space\n\n#### Core (Rust)\n\n**Codex Core** (&#96;codex-rs/core/&#96;):\n- AI assistant engine\n- Sub-agent orchestration\n- Deep research capabilities\n- MCP server integration\n\n**CLI** (&#96;codex-rs/cli/&#96;):\n- Command-line interface\n- TUI (Terminal UI) with GPU stats\n- Configuration management\n- Session handling\n- Plan mode support\n- CUDA acceleration\n\n**Tauri GUI** (&#96;codex-rs/tauri-gui/&#96;):\n- React + Three.js frontend\n- VR/AR integration (Quest 2/3/Pro, Vision Pro)\n- 4D Git visualization\n- Real-time GPU monitoring\n- Hand tracking support (Quest 3/Pro)\n\n#### Kernel Integration\n\n**Type-safe Rust APIs**:\n- &#96;ai-scheduler-rs&#96;: Scheduler logic\n- &#96;gpu-bindings&#96;: GPU operations\n- &#96;codex-ai-kernel-integration&#96;: /proc parser\n- &#96;codex-win-api&#96;: Windows driver API\n\n#### Repository Visualizer\n\n**Backend** (Rust + axum):\n- REST API (13 endpoints)",

        "contents": "/*\n * AI Memory Allocator\n * Kernel Module for AI-optimized memory management\n * \n * Features:\n * - Pinned memory pool (GPU accessible)\n * - Zero-copy transfers\n * - NUMA-aware allocation\n */\n\n#include &lt;linux/module.h&gt;\n#include &lt;linux/kernel.h&gt;\n#include &lt;linux/init.h&gt;\n#include &lt;linux/slab.h&gt;\n#include &lt;linux/mm.h&gt;\n#include &lt;linux/vmalloc.h&gt;\n#include &lt;linux/dma-mapping.h&gt;\n#include &lt;linux/proc_fs.h&gt;\n#include &lt;linux/seq_file.h&gt;\n\nMODULE_LICENSE(\"GPL\");\nMODULE_AUTHOR(\"zapabob\");\nMODULE_DESCRIPTION(\"AI Memory Allocator\");\nMODULE_VERSION(\"0.1.0\");\n\n// Memory pool configuration\n#define AI_MEM_POOL_SIZE (256 * 1024 * 1024)  // 256MB\n#define AI_MEM_BLOCK_SIZE (4 * 1024)          // 4KB blocks\n\nstruct ai_memory_block {\n    void *virt_addr;\n    dma_addr_t dma_addr;\n    size_t size;\n    bool is_allocated;\n    pid_t owner_pid;\n};\n\nstruct ai_memory_pool {\n    struct ai_memory_block *blocks;\n    int num_blocks;\n    spinlock_t lock;\n    atomic_t allocated_bytes;\n};\n\nstatic struct ai_memory_pool *global_pool = NULL;\n\n/*\n * Memory pool初期化\n */\nstatic int ai_mem_pool_init(void)\n{\n    int i;\n    int num_blocks = AI_MEM_POOL_SIZE / AI_MEM_BLOCK_SIZE;",

        "contents": "impl ResourceManager {\n    pub fn new() -&gt; Self {\n        // Default system resources (would be detected in real implementation)\n        let total_resources = ResourceAllocation {\n            cpu_cores: 8.0,\n            memory_mb: 16384, // 16GB\n            disk_gb: 500,\n            network_bandwidth_mbps: 1000,\n        };\n\n        Self {\n            total_resources,\n            allocated_resources: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub async fn check_availability(\n        &amp;self,\n        requested: &amp;ResourceAllocation,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;bool, Box&lt;dyn std::error::Error&gt;&gt; {\n        let allocated = self.allocated_resources.lock().unwrap();\n\n        let total_allocated = allocated.values().fold(\n            ResourceAllocation {\n                cpu_cores: 0.0,\n                memory_mb: 0,\n                disk_gb: 0,\n                network_bandwidth_mbps: 0,\n            },\n            |acc, res| ResourceAllocation {\n                cpu_cores: acc.cpu_cores + res.cpu_cores,\n                memory_mb: acc.memory_mb + res.memory_mb,\n                disk_gb: acc.disk_gb + res.disk_gb,\n                network_bandwidth_mbps: acc.network_bandwidth_mbps + res.network_bandwidth_mbps,\n            },\n        );\n\n        Ok(\n            total_allocated.cpu_cores + requested.cpu_cores &lt;= self.total_resources.cpu_cores\n                &amp;&amp; total_allocated.memory_mb + requested.memory_mb\n                    &lt;= self.total_resources.memory_mb\n                &amp;&amp; total_allocated.disk_gb + requested.disk_gb &lt;= self.total_resources.disk_gb\n                &amp;&amp; total_allocated.network_bandwidth_mbps + requested.network_bandwidth_mbps\n                    &lt;= self.total_resources.network_bandwidth_mbps,\n        )\n    }\n\n    pub async fn allocate_resources(\n        &amp;self,\n        env_id: &amp;str,",

        "contents": "impl PlanManager {\n    /// Create a new Plan manager\n    pub fn new() -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {\n        Ok(Self {\n            plans: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),\n            persister: PlanPersister::new()?,\n            policy_enforcer: PolicyEnforcer::default(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new Plan manager with custom persister and policy\n    pub fn with_config(persister: PlanPersister, policy_enforcer: PolicyEnforcer) -&gt; Self {\n        Self {\n            plans: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),\n            persister,\n            policy_enforcer,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new Plan\n    #[allow(non_snake_case)]\n    pub fn create_Plan(\n        &amp;self,\n        goal: String,\n        title: String,\n        created_by: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;String&gt; {\n        let mut bp = PlanBlock::new(goal, title);\n        bp.created_by = created_by;\n        bp.state = PlanState::Inactive.start_drafting()?;\n\n        let id = bp.id.clone();\n\n        // Store in memory\n        {\n            let mut plans = self.plans.write().unwrap();\n            plans.insert(id.clone(), bp.clone());\n        }\n\n        // Persist to disk\n        self.persister\n            .save_json(&amp;bp)\n            .context(\"Failed to persist Plan\")?;\n\n        Ok(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Get a Plan by ID\n    #[allow(non_snake_case)]\n    pub fn get_Plan(&amp;self, id: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;PlanBlock&gt; {\n        // Try memory first\n        {\n            let plans = self.plans.read().unwrap();\n            if let Some(bp) = plans.get(id) {\n                return Ok(bp.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Try loading from disk\n        let bp = self\n            .persister\n            .load_json(id)\n            .map_err(|_| ManagerError::NotFound { id: id.to_string() })?;\n\n        // Cache in memory\n        {\n            let mut plans = self.plans.write().unwrap();\n            plans.insert(id.to_string(), bp.clone());\n        }\n\n        Ok(bp)\n    }\n\n    /// Update a Plan (creates new version if scope changes)",

tokio::sync::mpsc;\nuse tokio::time::Duration;\nuse tokio::time::Instant;\nuse tokio::time::{self};\n\n/// Multi-AI tool orchestration system for parallel development\npub struct AIToolManager {\n    tools: HashMap&lt;String, AITool&gt;,\n    active_sessions: Mutex&lt;HashMap&lt;String, ActiveSession&gt;&gt;,\n    execution_engine: Arc&lt;AsyncExecutionEngine&gt;,\n    task_distributor:         "contents": "# Codex Project Overview\n\n## Purpose\nCodex is an AI-Native Operating System with 4D Git Visualization &amp; VR/AR Support. It's a Rust-based AI development platform that integrates multiple AI models, MCP servers, and provides advanced features like sub-agent orchestration, deep research capabilities, and cross-platform compatibility.\n\n## Tech Stack\n- **Language**: Rust 2024 edition\n- **Build System**: Cargo workspace with multiple crates\n- **Key Dependencies**: \n  - Async runtime (tokio, async-trait)\n  - MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers\n  - OpenTelemetry for tracing\n  - TUI libraries (ratatui)\n  - HTTP clients (reqwest)\n- **Platforms**: Windows, macOS, Linux, VR/AR support\n\n## Extended Features (zapabob/codex)\n- **Sub-Agent System**: Multi-agent orchestration with parallel execution (2.6x speedup)\n- **Deep Research Engine**: Multi-source research with citation management (45x speedup)\n- **MCP Server Extensions**: 7 additional tools and enhanced integration\n- **Orchestration Framework**: Advanced async execution patterns\n- **Cross-platform Sandboxing**: Enhanced Windows, macOS, Linux support\n\n## Code Structure\n- &#96;core/&#96;: Core functionality and orchestration\n- &#96;cli/&#96;: Command-line interface\n- &#96;tui/&#96;: Terminal user interface\n- &#96;app-server/&#96;: Backend server\n- &#96;mcp-server/&#96;: MCP server implementation\n- &#96;deep-research/&#96;: Research engine\n- &#96;agents/&#96;: Sub-agent system\n- Various utility crates and integrations\n\n## Development Commands\n- &#96;just fmt&#96;: Format code with rustfmt\n- &#96;just fix&#96;: Run clippy with auto-fix\n- &#96;just clippy&#96;: Run clippy linting\n- &#96;just test&#96;: Run tests with cargo-nextest\n- &#96;cargo check --all-features&#96;: Check compilation\n- &#96;cargo build --release&#96;: Release build\n- &#96;cargo install --path codex-rs/cli --force&#96;: Install CLI\n\n## Windows-Specific Notes\n- Use PowerShell instead of bash\n- Commands like &#96;cd codex-rs &amp;&amp; cargo check --all-features&#96; should be split (PowerShell doesn't support &amp;&amp;)\n- Build artifacts go to &#96;target/&#96; directory (should be in .gitignore)\n- Use &#96;cargo install&#96; for installing binaries",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "# AIネイティブOS カーネル拡張設計書\n\n**プロジェクト名**: Codex AI-Native OS Extensions  \n**バージョン**: 0.1.0-alpha  \n**日時**: 2025年11月2日  \n**目的**: OSカーネルレベルでAI推論を最適化し、AIネイティブな実行環境を構築\n\n---\n\n## 🎯 設計概要\n\n### ビジョン\n\n**AIワークロードに最適化されたOSカーネル拡張**を実装し、以下を実現：\n\n1. **GPU直接制御**: カーネル空間からGPU制御\n2. **AIスケジューラー**: ML推論に最適化されたプロセススケジューリング\n3. **専用メモリプール**: AI推論用の高速メモリアロケーター\n4. **システムコール拡張**: AI推論専用syscall追加\n5. **リアルタイムトレーシング**: eBPFベースのパフォーマンス監視\n\n### 対象OS\n\n| OS | カーネル拡張方式 | 実装難易度 |\n|----|----------------|-----------|\n| **Linux** | Kernel Module + eBPF | ⭐⭐⭐ (中) |\n| **Windows** | Kernel Driver (WDM/KMDF) | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (高) |\n| **macOS** | Kernel Extension (deprecated) | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (最高) |\n\n**優先順位**: Linux → Windows → macOS\n\n---\n\n## 🏗️ アーキテクチャ\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nUser Space\n├── Codex AI Assistant (Rust)\n├── AI Models (ONNX/TensorRT)\n└── User Applications\n    ↓ System Calls\n────────────────────────────────\nKernel Space\n├── AI Scheduler Module\n│   ├── GPU-aware scheduling\n│   ├── Priority queue for inference\n│   └── Latency optimization\n├── AI Memory Allocator\n│   ├── Pinned memory pool\n│   ├── Zero-copy transfer\n│   └── NUMA-aware allocation\n├── GPU Direct Access Module\n│   ├── CUDA driver integration\n│   ├── Vulkan compute interface\n│   └── ROCm support\n├── AI Syscall Extensions\n│   ├── sys_ai_infer() - 推論実行\n│   ├── sys_ai_alloc() - AI用メモリ確保\n│   └── sys_ai_trace() - パフォーマンストレース",

write!(f, \"failed to read file: {e}\"),\n            SkillParseError::MissingFrontmatter =&gt; {\n                write!(f, \"missing YAML frontmatter delimited by ---\")\n            }\n            SkillParseError::InvalidYaml(e) =&gt; write!(f, \"invalid YAML: {e}\"),\n            SkillParseError::MissingField(field) =&gt; write!(f, \"missing field &#96;{field}&#96;\"),\n            SkillParseError::InvalidField { field, reason } =&gt; {\n                write!(f, \"invalid {field}: {reason}\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Error for SkillParseError {}\n\npub fn load_skills(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; SkillLoadOutcome {\n    load_skills_from_roots(skill_roots(config))\n}\n\npub(crate) struct SkillRoot {\n    pub(crate) path: PathBuf,\n    pub(crate) scope: SkillScope,\n}\n\npub(crate) fn load_skills_from_roots&lt;I&gt;(roots: I) -&gt; SkillLoadOutcome\nwhere\n    I: IntoIterator&lt;Item = SkillRoot&gt;,\n{\n    let mut outcome = SkillLoadOutcome::default();\n    for root in roots {\n        discover_skills_under_root(&amp;root.path, root.scope, &amp;mut outcome);\n    }\n\n    let mut seen: HashSet&lt;String&gt; = HashSet::new();\n    outcome\n        .skills\n        .retain(|skill| seen.insert(skill.name.clone()));\n\n    outcome\n        .skills\n        .sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&amp;b.name).then_with(|| a.path.cmp(&amp;b.path)));\n\n    outcome\n}\n\npub(crate) fn user_skills_root(codex_home: &amp;Path) -&gt;         "contents": "// 主要機能\n- MemoryManager: 記憶の保存・検索・削除\n- MemoryStore: 永続化ストレージ（JSON/DB）\n- RetentionPolicy: 保持ポリシー（TTL、最大数）\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**メリット**:\n- ユーザー体験の大幅向上\n- プロジェクト固有の情報保持\n- コンテキストの連続性\n\n#### 1.2 Claude Sonnet 4.5 / Opus 4.5対応\n**目標**: 最新モデルの明示的サポート\n\n**実装内容**:\n- &#96;config.toml&#96;にモデル定義追加\n- モデル選択UI更新\n- パフォーマンステスト\n\n#### 1.3 Auto-Accept Mode UI\n**目標**: モード切り替えUI追加\n\n**実装内容**:\n- TUI/CLIに&#96;--auto-accept&#96;フラグ追加\n- VS Code拡張に設定追加\n- 承認ポリシー設定UI\n\n#### 1.4 Diagnostic Sharing\n**目標**: IDE診断エラーの自動共有\n\n**実装内容**:\n- DiagnosticCollector実装\n- IDE統合拡張\n- エージェントへの自動共有\n\n---\n\n### Phase 2: 中期（3-6ヶ月）⭐ **アーキテクチャ改善**\n\n#### 2.1 Agent Skills実装\n**目標**: スキルベースアーキテクチャへの移行\n\n**実装内容**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;rust\n// スキルベースアーキテクチャ\npub trait AgentSkill {\n    fn execute(&amp;self, context: &amp;SkillContext) -&gt; Result&lt;SkillResult&gt;;\n    fn metadata(&amp;self) -&gt; SkillMetadata;\n    fn dependencies(&amp;self) -&gt; Vec&lt;SkillId&gt;;\n}\n\n// スキルレジストリ\npub struct SkillRegistry {\n    skills: HashMap&lt;SkillId, Box&lt;dyn AgentSkill&gt;&gt;,\n    skill_graph: SkillDependencyGraph,\n}\n\n// 既存エージェントをスキルに分解\n// code-reviewer → [CodeReviewSkill, RustIdiomSkill, SecurityCheckSkill]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**メリット**:\n- 再利用性の向上\n- スキルの組み合わせによる柔軟性\n- 業界標準への準拠\n\n#### 2.2 Plan Mode Editing\n**目標**: 計画編集機能の実装\n\n**実装内容**:\n- PlanEditor実装\n- Diff表示機能\n- 段階的承認プロセス\n\n#### 2.3 Enterprise Governance\n**目標**: コンプライアンスとガバナンス機能",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\_docs\\2025-12-26_最新ClaudeCode調査_取り入れるべき機能まとめ.md",

            "line": 66
          }
        },
        "contents": "# 最新Claude Code調査レポート - Codex取り入れ推奨機能まとめ\n\n**調査日時**: 2025-12-26  \n**調査者**: AI Deep Researcher  \n**対象**: Claude Code最新機能（2024-2025）  \n**目的**: Codex v2.7.0への取り入れ推奨機能の特定\n\n---\n\n## 📊 エグゼクティブサマリー\n\n### 調査結果概要\n\n最新のClaude Code（2024-2025）で追加された主要機能を調査し、Codex v2.7.0の現状と比較分析しました。\n\n**調査範囲**:\n- Agent Skills（2025年10月）\n- Plan Mode with Editing\n- Memory Feature\n- Enterprise Integration\n- IDE統合強化\n- Claude Sonnet 4.5 / Opus 4.5対応\n\n**結論**: Codexは既に多くの機能を実装済みですが、**5つの重要な機能**を追加することで、さらに競争力が向上します。\n\n---\n\n## 🔍 最新Claude Codeの主要機能（2024-2025）\n\n### 1. Agent Skills（2025年10月）⭐ **高優先度**\n\n**概要**:\n- モジュラーなタスク特化コンポーネント\n- 再利用可能なスキルモジュール\n- Microsoft Visual Studio Code、GitHub統合\n- オープンソース化\n\n**特徴**:\n- タスク特化型の再利用可能モジュール\n- プラットフォーム統合（VS Code、GitHub）\n- 業界標準化を目指すオープンソースアプローチ\n\n**Codex現状**:\n- ✅ サブエージェント実装済み（researcher, test-gen, sec-audit, code-reviewer）\n- ✅ YAML定義によるカスタムエージェント\n- ⚠️ **スキルモジュール化が不足**（エージェント単位でのみ実装）\n\n**取り入れ推奨**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;rust\n// 推奨実装: スキルベースアーキテクチャ\npub trait AgentSkill {\n    fn execute(&amp;self, context: &amp;SkillContext) -&gt; Result&lt;SkillResult&gt;;\n    fn metadata(&amp;self) -&gt; SkillMetadata;\n}\n\npub struct SkillRegistry {\n    skills: HashMap&lt;String, Box&lt;dyn AgentSkill&gt;&gt;,\n}\n\n// 例: コードレビュースキル\npub struct CodeReviewSkill {\n    checks: Vec&lt;ReviewCheck&gt;,\n    severity_levels: SeverityConfig,\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# 最新Claude Code調査レポート - Codex取り入れ推奨機能まとめ",

            "text": "**対象**: Claude Code最新機能（2024-2025）  ",

            "text": "## 📊 エグゼクティブサマリー",

          {
            "text": "### 調査結果概要",
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "最新のClaude Code（2024-2025）で追加された主要機能を調査し、Codex v2.7.0の現状と比較分析しました。",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "text": "**調査範囲**:",
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "- Agent Skills（2025年10月）",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "text": "- Plan Mode with Editing",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "- Memory Feature",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "- Enterprise Integration",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "- IDE統合強化",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "- Claude Sonnet 4.5 / Opus 4.5対応",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "**結論**: Codexは既に多くの機能を実装済みですが、**5つの重要な機能**を追加することで、さらに競争力が向上します。",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "## 🔍 最新Claude Codeの主要機能（2024-2025）",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "### 1. Agent Skills（2025年10月）⭐ **高優先度**",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "**概要**:",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "- 再利用可能なスキルモジュール",

            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "text": "**Codex現状**:",
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ サブエージェント実装済み（researcher, test-gen, sec-audit, code-reviewer）",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ YAML定義によるカスタムエージェント",
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "- ⚠️ **スキルモジュール化が不足**（エージェント単位でのみ実装）",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "**取り入れ推奨**:",

          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;rust",
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "text": "// 推奨実装: スキルベースアーキテクチャ",
            "lineNumber": 50
          },

        "contents": "pub(crate) fn repo_skills_root(cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; Option&lt;SkillRoot&gt; {\n    let base = if cwd.is_dir() { cwd } else { cwd.parent()? };\n    let base = normalize_path(base).unwrap_or_else(|_| base.to_path_buf());\n\n    let repo_root =\n        resolve_root_git_project_for_trust(&amp;base).map(|root| normalize_path(&amp;root).unwrap_or(root));\n\n    let scope = SkillScope::Repo;\n    if let Some(repo_root) = repo_root.as_deref() {\n        for dir in base.ancestors() {\n            let skills_root = dir.join(REPO_ROOT_CONFIG_DIR_NAME).join(SKILLS_DIR_NAME);\n            if skills_root.is_dir() {\n                return Some(SkillRoot {\n                    path: skills_root,\n                    scope,\n                });\n            }\n\n            if dir == repo_root {\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let skills_root = base.join(REPO_ROOT_CONFIG_DIR_NAME).join(SKILLS_DIR_NAME);\n    skills_root.is_dir().then_some(SkillRoot {\n        path: skills_root,\n        scope,\n    })\n}\n\npub(crate) fn skill_roots_for_cwd(codex_home: &amp;Path, cwd: &amp;Path) -&gt; Vec&lt;SkillRoot&gt; {\n    let mut roots = Vec::new();\n\n    if let Some(repo_root) = repo_skills_root(cwd) {\n        roots.push(repo_root);\n    }\n\n    // Load order matters: we dedupe by name, keeping the first occurrence.\n    // Priority order: repo, user, system, then admin.\n    roots.push(user_skills_root(codex_home));\n    roots.push(system_skills_root(codex_home));\n    if cfg!(unix) {\n        roots.push(admin_skills_root());\n    }\n\n    roots\n}\n\nfn skill_roots(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; Vec&lt;SkillRoot&gt; {\n    skill_roots_for_cwd(&amp;config.codex_home, &amp;config.cwd)\n}\n\nfn discover_skills_under_root(root: &amp;Path, scope: SkillScope,",

        "contents": "use serde::Deserialize;\nuse serde::Serialize;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\n\n/// サブエージェントの定義\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]\npub struct AgentDefinition {\n    /// エージェント名\n    pub name: String,\n    /// エージェントの目標\n    pub goal: String,\n    /// 詳細なインストラクション（LLMに渡されるシステムプロンプトの一部）\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub instructions: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    /// ツール権限\n    pub tools: ToolPermissions,\n    /// ポリシー設定\n    pub policies: AgentPolicies,\n    /// 成功基準\n    pub success_criteria: Vec&lt;String&gt;,\n    /// 出力アーティファクト\n    pub artifacts: Vec&lt;String&gt;,\n    /// エージェント固有の設定\n    #[serde(flatten)]\n    pub extra: HashMap&lt;String, serde_json::Value&gt;,\n}\n\n/// ツール権限設定\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]\npub struct ToolPermissions {\n    /// MCPツールの許可リスト\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub mcp: Vec&lt;String&gt;,\n    /// ファイルシステム権限\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub fs: FsPermissions,\n    /// ネットワーク権限\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub net: NetPermissions,\n    /// シェル実行権限\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub shell: ShellPermissions,\n}\n\n/// ファイルシステム権限\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Default)]\npub struct FsPermissions {\n    /// 読み取り権限\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub read: bool,\n    /// 書き込み権限（パスのリスト）\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub write: FsWritePermission,\n}\n\n/// ファイル書き込み権限\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]\n#[serde(untagged)]\npub enum FsWritePermission {\n    /// 全体の許可フラグ\n    Flag(bool),\n    /// 許可されたパスのリスト\n    Paths(Vec&lt;String&gt;),\n}\n\nimpl Default for FsWritePermission {\n    fn default() -&gt; Self",

        },
        "contents": "use crate::skills::model::SkillMetadata;\n\npub fn render_skills_section(skills: &amp;[SkillMetadata]) -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {\n    if skills.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let mut lines: Vec&lt;String&gt; = Vec::new();\n    lines.push(\"## Skills\".to_string());\n    lines.push(\"These skills are discovered at startup from multiple local sources. Each entry includes a name, description, and file path so you can open the source for full instructions.\".to_string());\n\n    for skill in skills {\n        let path_str = skill.path.to_string_lossy().replace('\\\\', \"/\");\n        let name = skill.name.as_str();\n        let description = skill.description.as_str();\n        lines.push(format!(\"- {name}: {description} (file: {path_str})\"));\n    }\n\n    lines.push(\n        r###\"- Discovery: Available skills are listed in project docs and may also appear in a runtime \"## Skills\" section (name + description + file path). These are the sources of truth; skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths.\n- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with &#96;$SkillName&#96; or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.\n- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.\n- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):\n  1) After deciding to use a skill, open its &#96;SKILL.md&#96;. Read only enough to follow the workflow.\n  2) If &#96;SKILL.md&#96; points to extra folders such as &#96;references/&#96;, load only the specific files needed for the request; don't bulk-load everything.\n  3) If &#96;scripts/&#96; exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.\n  4) If &#96;assets/&#96; or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.\n- Description as trigger: The YAML &#96;description&#96; in &#96;SKILL.md&#96; is the primary trigger signal; rely on it to decide applicability. If unsure, ask a brief clarification before proceeding.\n- Coordination and sequencing:\n  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.\n  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.\n- Context hygiene:\n  - Keep context small: summarize long sections instead of pasting them; only load extra files when needed.\n  - Avoid deeply nested references; prefer one-hop files explicitly linked from &#96;SKILL.md&#96;.\n  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.\n- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.\"###\n            .to_string(),\n    );\n\n    Some(lines.join(\"\\n\"))\n}",

        "contents": "use std::collections::HashSet;\n\nuse crate::skills::SkillLoadOutcome;\nuse crate::skills::SkillMetadata;\nuse crate::user_instructions::SkillInstructions;\nuse codex_protocol::models::ResponseItem;\nuse codex_protocol::user_input::UserInput;\nuse tokio::fs;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub(crate) struct SkillInjections {\n    pub(crate) items: Vec&lt;ResponseItem&gt;,\n    pub(crate) warnings: Vec&lt;String&gt;,\n}\n\npub(crate) async fn build_skill_injections(\n    inputs: &amp;[UserInput],\n    skills: Option&lt;&amp;SkillLoadOutcome&gt;,\n) -&gt; SkillInjections {\n    if inputs.is_empty() {\n        return SkillInjections::default();\n    }\n\n    let Some(outcome) = skills else {\n        return SkillInjections::default();\n    };\n\n    let mentioned_skills = collect_explicit_skill_mentions(inputs, &amp;outcome.skills);\n    if mentioned_skills.is_empty() {\n        return SkillInjections::default();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = SkillInjections {\n        items: Vec::with_capacity(mentioned_skills.len()),\n        warnings: Vec::new(),\n    };\n\n    for skill in mentioned_skills {\n        match fs::read_to_string(&amp;skill.path).await {\n            Ok(contents) =&gt; {\n                result.items.push(ResponseItem::from(SkillInstructions {\n                    name: skill.name,\n                    path: skill.path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),\n                    contents,\n                }));\n            }\n            Err(err) =&gt; {\n                let message = format!(\n                    \"Failed to load skill {} at {}: {err:#}\",\n                    skill.name,\n                    skill.path.display()\n                );\n                result.warnings.push(message);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    result\n}\n\nfn collect_explicit_skill_mentions",

        "contents": "impl RealSubAgentManager {\n    pub fn new(model: String) -&gt; Self {\n        Self {\n            agents: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            model,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn register_agent(&amp;mut self, agent_type: AgentType) {\n        let agent = RealSubAgent::new(agent_type.clone(), self.model.clone());\n        self.agents.insert(agent_type, agent);\n    }\n\n    pub async fn dispatch_task(&amp;mut self, agent_type: AgentType, task: String) -&gt; Result&lt;String&gt; {\n        let agent = self\n            .agents\n            .get_mut(&amp;agent_type)\n            .context(\"Agent not found\")?;\n        agent.process_task(task).await\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_agent_state(&amp;self, agent_type: &amp;AgentType) -&gt; Option&lt;AgentState&gt; {\n        self.agents.get(agent_type).map(|a| a.get_state())\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_all_states(&amp;self) -&gt; Vec&lt;AgentState&gt; {\n        self.agents.values().map(|a| a.get_state()).collect()\n    }\n\n    pub async fn broadcast_message(&amp;self, message: AgentMessage) -&gt; Result&lt;()&gt; {\n        for agent in self.agents.values() {\n            agent.send_message(message.clone()).await?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Register all default agents\n    pub fn register_all_agents(&amp;mut self) {\n        self.register_agent(AgentType::CodeExpert);\n        self.register_agent(AgentType::SecurityExpert);\n        self.register_agent(AgentType::TestingExpert);\n        self.register_agent(AgentType::DocsExpert);\n        self.register_agent(AgentType::DeepResearcher);\n        self.register_agent(AgentType::DebugExpert);\n        self.register_agent(AgentType::PerformanceExpert);\n        self.register_agent(AgentType::General);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for RealSubAgentManager {\n    fn default() -&gt; Self {\n        let mut manager = Self::new(\"gpt-4o-mini\".to_string());\n        manager.register_all_agents();\n        manager\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use pretty_assertions::assert_eq;",

        "contents": "//! Plan manager\n//!\n//! High-level API for creating, updating, approving, and exporting plan.\n\nuse super::persist::PlanPersister;\nuse super::policy::ApprovalRole;\nuse super::policy::PolicyEnforcer;\nuse super::policy::PrivilegedOperation;\nuse super::schema::PlanBlock;\nuse super::schema::ResearchBlock;\nuse super::schema::Risk;\nuse super::schema::WorkItem;\nuse super::state::PlanState;\nuse super::state::StateTransitionError;\nuse anyhow::Context;\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::sync::RwLock;\nuse thiserror::Error;\n\n/// Errors from Plan manager operations\n#[derive(Debug, Error)]\npub enum ManagerError {\n    #[error(\"Plan not found: {id}\")]\n    NotFound { id: String },\n\n    #[error(\"Plan cannot be modified in current state: {state}\")]\n    CannotModify { state: String },\n\n    #[error(\"State transition error: {0}\")]\n    StateTransition(#[from] StateTransitionError),\n\n    #[error(\"Persistence error: {0}\")]\n    Persistence(#[from] std::io::Error),\n\n    #[error(\"Policy violation: {0}\")]\n    Policy(#[from] super::policy::PolicyError),\n}\n\n/// Plan manager for high-level operations\npub struct PlanManager {\n    /// In-memory Plan store\n    plans: Arc&lt;RwLock&lt;HashMap&lt;String, PlanBlock&gt;&gt;&gt;,\n\n    /// Persister for saving Plans\n    persister: PlanPersister,\n\n    /// Policy enforcer\n    policy_enforcer: PolicyEnforcer,\n}\n\nimpl PlanManager {\n    /// Create a new Plan manager",

        "contents": "# plan mode - User Guide\n\n**Version**: 0.57.0  \n**Status**: Production Ready\n\n---\n\n## 📖 Table of Contents\n\n1. [Overview](#overview)\n2. [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n3. [Slash Commands](#slash-commands)\n4. [GUI Controls](#gui-controls)\n5. [Execution Modes](#execution-modes)\n6. [Deep Research Integration](#deep-research-integration)\n7. [Webhook Notifications](#webhook-notifications)\n8. [Examples](#examples)\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\n**plan mode** is a read-only planning phase that lets you design and review changes before execution. It provides:\n\n- ✅ **Approval Gates**: No side effects until explicitly approved\n- ✅ **Multiple Execution Strategies**: Single, Orchestrated, or Competition\n- ✅ **Deep Research**: Integrated research with citations\n- ✅ **Budget Enforcement**: Token and time limits\n- ✅ **Webhook Notifications**: GitHub, Slack, HTTP integrations\n- ✅ **Telemetry**: Privacy-respecting event collection\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Enable plan mode\n\n**CLI**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncodex /Plan on\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**VS Code**:\n- Press &#96;Shift+Tab&#96; (toggle)\n- Or: Command Palette → &#96;Codex: Toggle plan mode&#96;\n\n### Create a Plan\n\n**CLI**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncodex /Plan \"Add request logging\" --mode=orchestrated\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**VS Code**:\n- Command Palette → &#96;Codex: Create Plan&#96;\n- Enter title and goal\n\n### Approve &amp; Execute\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Review the Plan\ncodex /Plan export bp-123 --format=md\n\n# Approve\ncodex /approve bp-123\n\n# Execute (now unlocked)\ncodex execute bp-123\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Slash Commands\n\n### &#96;/Plan on|off&#96;\n\nToggle plan mode.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncodex /Plan on   # Enter plan mode\ncodex /Plan off  # Exit plan mode\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### &#96;/Plan \"&lt;title&gt;\" [options]&#96;\n\nCreate a new Plan.\n\n**Options**:\n- &#96;--mode=single|orchestrated|competition&#96; (default: orchestrated)\n- &#96;--budget.tokens=&lt;number&gt;&#96; (default: 100000)\n- &#96;--budget.time=&lt;minutes&gt;&#96; (default: 30)\n\n**Examples**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Simple feature\ncodex /Plan \"Add logging middleware\" --mode=single\n\n# Orchestrated refactor\ncodex /Plan \"Refactor auth system\" --mode=orchestrated --budget.tokens=150000\n\n# Performance competition\ncodex /Plan \"Optimize DB query\" --mode=competition",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "# plan mode - User Guide\n\n**Version**: 0.57.0  \n**Status**: Production Ready\n\n---\n\n## 📖 Table of Contents\n\n1. [Overview](#overview)\n2. [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n3. [Slash Commands](#slash-commands)\n4. [GUI Controls](#gui-controls)\n5. [Execution Modes](#execution-modes)\n6. [Deep Research Integration](#deep-research-integration)\n7. [Webhook Notifications](#webhook-notifications)\n8. [Examples](#examples)\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\n**plan mode** is a read-only planning phase that lets you design and review changes before execution. It provides:\n\n- ✅ **Approval Gates**: No side effects until explicitly approved\n- ✅ **Multiple Execution Strategies**: Single, Orchestrated, or Competition\n- ✅ **Deep Research**: Integrated research with citations\n- ✅ **Budget Enforcement**: Token and time limits\n- ✅ **Webhook Notifications**: GitHub, Slack, HTTP integrations\n- ✅ **Telemetry**: Privacy-respecting event collection\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Enable plan mode\n\n**CLI**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncodex /Plan on\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**VS Code**:\n- Press &#96;Shift+Tab&#96; (toggle)\n- Or: Command Palette → &#96;Codex: Toggle plan mode&#96;\n\n### Create a Plan\n\n**CLI**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncodex /Plan \"Add request logging\" --mode=orchestrated\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**VS Code**:\n- Command Palette → &#96;Codex: Create Plan&#96;\n- Enter title and goal\n\n### Approve &amp; Execute\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Review the Plan\ncodex /Plan export bp-123 --format=md\n\n# Approve\ncodex /approve bp-123\n\n# Execute (now unlocked)\ncodex execute bp-123\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Slash Commands\n\n### &#96;/Plan on|off&#96;\n\nToggle plan mode.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncodex /Plan on   # Enter plan mode\ncodex /Plan off  # Exit plan mode\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### &#96;/Plan \"&lt;title&gt;\" [options]&#96;\n\nCreate a new Plan.\n\n**Options**:\n- &#96;--mode=single|orchestrated|competition&#96; (default: orchestrated)\n- &#96;--budget.tokens=&lt;number&gt;&#96; (default: 100000)\n- &#96;--budget.time=&lt;minutes&gt;&#96; (default: 30)\n\n**Examples**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Simple feature\ncodex /Plan \"Add logging middleware\" --mode=single\n\n# Orchestrated refactor\ncodex /Plan \"Refactor auth system\" --mode=orchestrated --budget.tokens=150000\n\n# Performance competition\ncodex /Plan \"Optimize DB query\" --mode=competition",

        "contents": "impl PlanManager {\n    /// Create a new Plan manager\n    pub fn new() -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {\n        Ok(Self {\n            plans: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),\n            persister: PlanPersister::new()?,\n            policy_enforcer: PolicyEnforcer::default(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new Plan manager with custom persister and policy\n    pub fn with_config(persister: PlanPersister, policy_enforcer: PolicyEnforcer) -&gt; Self {\n        Self {\n            plans: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),\n            persister,\n            policy_enforcer,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new Plan\n    #[allow(non_snake_case)]\n    pub fn create_Plan(\n        &amp;self,\n        goal: String,\n        title: String,\n        created_by: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;String&gt; {\n        let mut bp = PlanBlock::new(goal, title);\n        bp.created_by = created_by;\n        bp.state = PlanState::Inactive.start_drafting()?;\n\n        let id = bp.id.clone();\n\n        // Store in memory\n        {\n            let mut plans = self.plans.write().unwrap();\n            plans.insert(id.clone(), bp.clone());\n        }\n\n        // Persist to disk\n        self.persister\n            .save_json(&amp;bp)\n            .context(\"Failed to persist Plan\")?;\n\n        Ok(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Get a Plan by ID\n    #[allow(non_snake_case)]\n    pub fn get_Plan(&amp;self, id: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;PlanBlock&gt; {\n        // Try memory first\n        {\n            let plans = self.plans.read().unwrap();\n            if let Some(bp) = plans.get(id) {\n                return Ok(bp.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Try loading from disk\n        let bp = self\n            .persister\n            .load_json(id)\n            .map_err(|_| ManagerError::NotFound { id: id.to_string() })?;\n\n        // Cache in memory\n        {\n            let mut plans = self.plans.write().unwrap();\n            plans.insert(id.to_string(), bp.clone());\n        }\n\n        Ok(bp)\n    }\n\n    /// Update a Plan (creates new version if scope changes)",

        "contents": "impl PlanManager {\n    /// Create a new Plan manager\n    pub fn new() -&gt; Result&lt;Self&gt; {\n        Ok(Self {\n            plans: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),\n            persister: PlanPersister::new()?,\n            policy_enforcer: PolicyEnforcer::default(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new Plan manager with custom persister and policy\n    pub fn with_config(persister: PlanPersister, policy_enforcer: PolicyEnforcer) -&gt; Self {\n        Self {\n            plans: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),\n            persister,\n            policy_enforcer,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new Plan\n    #[allow(non_snake_case)]\n    pub fn create_Plan(\n        &amp;self,\n        goal: String,\n        title: String,\n        created_by: Option&lt;String&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;String&gt; {\n        let mut bp = PlanBlock::new(goal, title);\n        bp.created_by = created_by;\n        bp.state = PlanState::Inactive.start_drafting()?;\n\n        let id = bp.id.clone();\n\n        // Store in memory\n        {\n            let mut plans = self.plans.write().unwrap();\n            plans.insert(id.clone(), bp.clone());\n        }\n\n        // Persist to disk\n        self.persister\n            .save_json(&amp;bp)\n            .context(\"Failed to persist Plan\")?;\n\n        Ok(id)\n    }\n\n    /// Get a Plan by ID\n    #[allow(non_snake_case)]\n    pub fn get_Plan(&amp;self, id: &amp;str) -&gt; Result&lt;PlanBlock&gt; {\n        // Try memory first\n        {\n            let plans = self.plans.read().unwrap();\n            if let Some(bp) = plans.get(id) {\n                return Ok(bp.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Try loading from disk\n        let bp = self\n            .persister\n            .load_json(id)\n            .map_err(|_| ManagerError::NotFound { id: id.to_string() })?;\n\n        // Cache in memory\n        {\n            let mut plans = self.plans.write().unwrap();\n            plans.insert(id.to_string(), bp.clone());\n        }\n\n        Ok(bp)\n    }\n\n    /// Update a Plan (creates new version if scope changes)",

        "contents": "'use client'\n\nimport { useEffect, useState } from 'react'\nimport {\n  listPlans,\n  createPlan,\n  approvePlan,\n  rejectPlan,\n  exportPlan,\n  togglePlanMode,\n  type Plan,\n  type CreatePlanRequest,\n} from '../../../lib/api/Plans'\nimport { useplanStore } from '../../../lib/stores/planStore'\n\nexport default function PlansPage() {\n  const {\n    isEnabled,\n    Plans,\n    selectedPlan,\n    loading,\n    error,\n    setEnabled,\n    setPlans,\n    setSelectedPlan,\n    setLoading,\n    setError,\n  } = useplanStore()\n\n  const [showCreateModal, setShowCreateModal] = useState(false)\n  const [filterState, setFilterState] = useState&lt;string | undefined&gt;(undefined)\n\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    loadPlans()\n  }, [filterState])\n\n  const loadPlans = async () =&gt; {\n    setLoading(true)\n    setError(null)\n    try {\n      const data = await listPlans(filterState)\n      setPlans(data)\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to load Plans')\n    } finally {\n      setLoading(false)\n    }\n  }\n\n  const handleToggleMode = async () =&gt; {\n    try {\n      const newState = !isEnabled\n      await togglePlanMode(newState)\n      setEnabled(newState)\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to toggle mode')\n    }\n  }\n\n  const handleCreatePlan = async (data: CreatePlanRequest) =&gt; {\n    try {\n      await createPlan(data)\n      await loadPlans()\n      setShowCreateModal(false)\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to create Plan')\n    }\n  }\n\n  const handleApprove = async (id: string) =&gt; {\n    try {\n      await approvePlan(id)\n      await loadPlans()\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to approve Plan')\n    }\n  }\n\n  const handleReject = async (id: string, reason: string) =&gt; {\n    try {\n      await rejectPlan(id, reason)\n      await loadPlans()\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to reject Plan')\n    }\n  }\n\n  const handleExport = async (id: string, format: 'md' | 'json' | 'both')\n\n}",

        "contents": "export const PlanCreator: React.FC&lt;PlanCreatorProps&gt; = \n\n\n  const handleCreatePlan = async () =&gt; {\n    if (!newPlan.title.trim()) return;\n\n    try {\n      setIsLoading(true);\n      const result = await apiClient.createPlan({\n        title: newPlan.title,\n        mode: newPlan.mode,\n        budgetTokens: newPlan.budgetTokens,\n        budgetTime: newPlan.budgetTime,\n      });\n\n      const createdPlan: Plan = {\n        id: result.id || &#96;plan-${Date.now()}&#96;,\n        title: result.title || newPlan.title,\n        mode: result.mode || newPlan.mode,\n        budgetTokens: result.budgetTokens || newPlan.budgetTokens,\n        budgetTime: result.budgetTime || newPlan.budgetTime,\n        state: result.state || 'drafting',\n        createdAt: result.createdAt ? new Date(result.createdAt) : new Date(),\n        updatedAt: result.updatedAt ? new Date(result.updatedAt) : new Date(),\n      };\n\n      setPlans([createdPlan, ...plans]);\n      setCreateDialogOpen(false);\n      setNewPlan({ title: '', mode: 'orchestrated', budgetTokens: 100000, budgetTime: 30 });\n      onPlanCreated?.(createdPlan);\n    } catch (error) {\n      console.error('Failed to create plan:', error);\n    } finally {\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const handleApprovePlan = async (planId: string) =&gt; {\n    try {\n      setIsLoading(true);\n      await apiClient.approvePlan(planId);\n      \n      setPlans(plans.map(p =&gt; \n        p.id === planId ? { ...p, state: 'approved' as const, updatedAt: new Date() } : p\n      ));\n    } catch (error) {\n      console.error('Failed to approve plan:', error);\n    } finally {\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const handleExecutePlan = async (planId: string) =&gt;\n;\n;",

                {
                  "lineNumber": 12,
                  "content": "## About Skills"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 14,
                  "content": "Skills are modular, self-contained packages that extend Codex's capabilities by providing"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 19,
                  "content": "### What Skills Provide"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 30,
                  "content": "The context window is a public good. Skills share the context window with everything else Codex needs: system prompt, conversation history, other Skills' metadata, and the actual user request."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 48,
                  "content": "### Anatomy of a Skill"
                },

                  "lineNumber": 50,

                  "lineNumber": 69,
                  "content": "- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains &#96;name&#96; and &#96;description&#96; fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 70,
                  "content": "- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all)."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 90,
                  "content": "- **Benefits**: Keeps SKILL.md lean, loaded only when Codex determines it's needed"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 91,
                  "content": "- **Best practice**: If files are large (&gt;10k words), include grep search patterns in SKILL.md"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 92,
                  "content": "- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 98,
                  "content": "- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 103,
                  "content": "#### What to Not Include in a Skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 105,
                  "content": "A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:"
                },

                  "lineNumber": 113,
                  "content": "The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion."
                },

                  "lineNumber": 117,
                  "content": "Skills use a three-level loading system to manage context efficiently:"

                  "lineNumber": 120,

When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them."
                },

                  "lineNumber": 127,
                  "content": "**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files."

                {
                  "lineNumber": 200,

                {
                  "lineNumber": 203,
                  "content": "## Skill Creation Process"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 205,
                  "content": "Skill creation involves these steps:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 207,
                  "content": "1. Understand the skill with concrete examples"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 208,
                  "content": "2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 209,
                  "content": "3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 210,
                  "content": "4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 211,
                  "content": "5. Package the skill (run package_skill.py)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 216,
                  "content": "### Skill Naming"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 222,
                  "content": "- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 224,
                  "content": "### Step 1: Understanding the Skill with Concrete Examples"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 226,
                  "content": "Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 228,
                  "content": "To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 230,
                  "content": "For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 232,
                  "content": "- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 233,
                  "content": "- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 234,
                  "content": "- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 235,
                  "content": "- \"What would a user say that should trigger this skill?\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 239,
                  "content": "Conclude this step when there is a clear sense of the functionality the skill should support."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 241,
                  "content": "### Step 2: Planning the Reusable Skill Contents"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 243,
                  "content": "To turn concrete examples into an effective skill, analyze each example by:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 248,
                  "content": "Example: When building a &#96;pdf-editor&#96; skill to handle queries like \"Help me rotate this PDF,\" the analysis shows:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 251,
                  "content": "2. A &#96;scripts/rotate_pdf.py&#96; script would be helpful to store in the skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 253,
                  "content": "Example: When designing a &#96;frontend-webapp-builder&#96; skill for queries like \"Build me a todo app\" or \"Build me a dashboard to track my steps,\" the analysis shows:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 256,
                  "content": "2. An &#96;assets/hello-world/&#96; template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 258,
                  "content": "Example: When building a &#96;big-query&#96; skill to handle queries like \"How many users have logged in today?\" the analysis shows:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 261,
                  "content": "2. A &#96;references/schema.md&#96; file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 263,
                  "content": "To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 265,
                  "content": "### Step 3: Initializing the Skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 267,
                  "content": "At this point, it is time to actually create the skill."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 269,
                  "content": "Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists, and iteration or packaging is needed. In this case, continue to the next step."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 271,
                  "content": "When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the &#96;init_skill.py&#96; script.                 },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 276,

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 282,
                  "content": "scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path skills/public"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 283,
                  "content": "scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path skills/public --resources scripts,references"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 284,
                  "content": "scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path skills/public --resources scripts --examples"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 289,
                  "content": "- Creates the skill directory at the specified path"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 290,
                  "content": "- Generates a SKILL.md template with proper frontmatter and TODO placeholders"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 294,
                  "content": "After initialization, customize the SKILL.md and add resources as needed. If you used &#96;--examples&#96;, replace or delete placeholder files."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 296,
                  "content": "### Step 4: Edit the Skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 298,
                  "content": "When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 302,
                  "content": "Consult these helpful guides based on your skill's needs:"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 307,
                  "content": "These files contain established best practices for effective skill design."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 309,
                  "content": "#### Start with Reusable Skill Contents"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 311,
                  "content": "To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: &#96;scripts/&#96;, &#96;references/&#96;, and &#96;assets/&#96; files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a &#96;brand-guidelines&#96; skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in &#96;assets/&#96;, or documentation to store in &#96;references/&#96;."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 315,
                  "content": "If you used &#96;--examples&#96;, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 317,
                  "content": "#### Update SKILL.md"

                {
                  "lineNumber": 325,

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 326,
                  "content": "- &#96;description&#96;: This is the primary triggering mechanism for your skill, and helps Codex understand when to use the skill."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 327,
                  "content": "  - Include both what the Skill does and specific triggers/contexts for when to use it."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 328,
                  "content": "  - Include all \"when to use\" information here - Not in the body. The body is only loaded after triggering, so \"When to Use This Skill\" sections in the body are not helpful to Codex."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 329,
                  "content": "  - Example description for a &#96;docx&#96; skill: \"Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction.                 },
                {

                  "content": "Write instructions for using the skill and its bundled resources."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 337,
                  "content": "### Step 5: Packaging a Skill"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 339,
                  "content": "Once development of the skill is complete, it must be packaged into a distributable .skill file that gets shared with the user. The packaging process automatically validates the skill first to ensure it meets all requirements:"

                  "lineNumber": 348,

                  "lineNumber": 353,

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 360,
                  "content": "2. **Package** the skill if validation passes, creating a .skill file named after the skill (e.g., &#96;my-skill.skill&#96;) that includes all files and maintains the proper directory structure for distribution. The .skill file is a zip file with a .skill extension."
                },

        "contents": "# Blueprint Mode v0.57.0 実装完了レポート 🎉\n\n**実装日**: 2025-11-02  \n**担当**: Cursor Agent (zapabob/codex)  \n**バージョン**: v0.57.0-alpha → v0.57.0-beta  \n**進捗**: 17/24 TODOs完了 (71%)\n\n---\n\n## 🏆 実装サマリー\n\n### ✅ 完了した主要機能 (17/24 = 71%)\n\n**Rust Backend (Core Infrastructure)**:\n1. ✅ Blueprint Core Module (schema, state, persist, policy, budget, manager)\n2. ✅ Orchestrator RPC Extensions (8 new methods)\n3. ✅ Execution Engine (mode switching)\n4. ✅ Worktree Competition (manager, scorer, merger)\n5. ✅ DeepResearch Integration (approval dialog, ResearchBlock)\n6. ✅ Telemetry Module (events, collector, storage)\n7. ✅ Webhooks Module (GitHub, Slack, HTTP)\n8. ✅ Linter Fixes (orchestrator warnings解消)\n\n**TypeScript Frontend (VS Code Extension)**:\n9. ✅ Blueprint State Management\n10. ✅ Slash Commands (/blueprint, /approve, /reject, /mode, /deepresearch)\n11. ✅ Status Badge (color-coded state indicators)\n12. ✅ UI Components (statusBar, views)\n13. ✅ VS Code Settings &amp; Keybindings (Shift+Tab)\n\n**Documentation &amp; Tools**:\n14. ✅ User Documentation (README, slash-commands, execution-modes, webhooks)\n15. ✅ Developer Documentation (architecture)\n16. ✅ Sample Blueprints (3 examples)\n17. ✅ Migration Script (plans → blueprints)\n18. ✅ CHANGELOG v0.57.0\n\n### ⏳ 残りTODOs (7/24 = 29%)\n\n**Optional Enhancements**:\n- ⏳ Orchestrated Enhancement (telemetry/webhook emission from AutoOrchestrator)\n- ⏳ GUI Toolbar (Enter Blueprint button等)\n- ⏳ Approval Dialog (modal dialog for research)\n\n**Testing** (後で追加可能):\n- ⏳ Rust Unit Tests (既に各moduleに組み込み済み)\n- ⏳ Rust Integration Tests\n- ⏳ TypeScript Tests\n- ⏳ E2E Tests\n\n---\n\n## 📊 実装統計\n\n### コード行数\n\n#### Rust Backend\n\n| Module | Files | Lines | Tests | Structs/Enums |\n|--------|-------|-------|-------|---------------|\n| **Blueprint Core** | 7 | 2,564 | 500 | 25 |\n| blueprint/schema.rs | 1 | 312 | 25 | 10 |\n| blueprint/state.rs | 1 | 250 | 90 | 2 |",

        "contents": "### 🙏 Acknowledgments\n\n- Based on [OpenAI/codex](https://github.com/openai/codex)\n- Extended by [@zapabob](https://github.com/zapabob)\n- Inspired by Kamui4D project\n\n---\n\n&lt;a name=\"japanese\"&gt;&lt;/a&gt;\n## 📖 日本語\n\n### 🎉 v2.7.0 \"Version Unification &amp; Skills/Plan Alignment\" の新機能\n\n**リリース日**: 2025年12月21日\n**マイルストーン**: バージョン統一 &amp; 公式Skills/Plan整合\n\n**🎁 v2.7.0の新機能**:\n- ✅ **バージョン統一**: すべてのpackage.jsonファイルとRustワークスペースをバージョン2.7.0に統一\n- ✅ **Skills/Plan整合**: 公式Plan Modeドキュメントに合わせてplan skillを調整\n- ✅ **依存関係のモダン化**: PythonヘルパーをRust/TypeScript実装に置き換え\n- ✅ **Planストレージ統一**: planストレージディレクトリ名を統一（&#96;plans&#96; vs &#96;Plans&#96;の不一致を解決）\n- ✅ **公式コマンド統合**: 公式Plan Modeコマンド（&#96;/Plan&#96;、&#96;/approve&#96;、&#96;/Plan export&#96;）を使用するように更新\n- ✅ **Python依存関係の削除**: plan skillからすべてのPythonスクリプト依存関係を削除\n\n**📋 以前のアップデート（v2.5.0 - v2.6.0）**:\n- ✅ **公式リポジトリ統合**: OpenAI/codexの最新機能、セキュリティ修正、バグ修正を統合\n- ✅ **Unified Execシステム**: 非同期ウォッチャーと改善されたセッション管理による実行環境強化\n- ✅ **セキュリティ強化**: MCP SDK v1.24.0更新、サンドボックスと権限管理の改善\n- ✅ **Windowsサンドボックス改善**: ConPTYサポートとWindows固有のサンドボックス強化\n- ✅ **パフォーマンス最適化**: 高速インクリメンタルビルドと最適化された非同期実行パターン\n- ✅ **クロスプラットフォーム互換性**: Windows、macOS、Linuxのサポート改善\n- ✅ **CI/CDパイプライン更新**: GitHub Actionsワークフロー更新 (actions/checkout@v6)\n- ✅ **ゼロエラーポリシー**: すべてのコードがゼロエラー/警告で合格 (Rust 2024 edition)\n\n#### 🌟 革命的機能\n\n**🎯 プランモード (Blueprint→Plan移行完了)**",

        "contents": "# Codex v2.4.0 Release Notes\n\n## Overview\nCodex v2.4.0 \"AI Orchestration &amp; Testing Suite\" introduces comprehensive AI orchestration capabilities and automated testing infrastructure.\n\n## What's New in v2.4.0\n\n### ､・AI Orchestration Engine\n- Multi-layered research pipeline for intelligent code analysis\n- Centralized task manager coordinating sub-agents\n- Advanced agent coordination and collaboration systems\n\n### ｧｮ Mathematical &amp; Quantum Optimization\n- Linear programming algorithms for mathematical optimization\n- QAOA-inspired quantum optimization for code selection\n- Automated quality metrics evaluation\n\n### 諺 Git Worktree Parallel Development\n- Automated worktree management for parallel development\n- Intelligent conflict resolution algorithms\n- AI-powered merge conflict assistance\n\n### 識 QC Agent Quality Control\n- Automated testing and validation systems\n- Quality metrics collection and analysis\n- Optimal code selection algorithms\n\n### 箕・・MacOS-style Virtual OS\n- CLI app creation and management\n- Security monitoring and access control\n- GitHub integration with webhook support\n\n### 町 LINE Bidirectional Communication\n- Interactive LINE-based development interface\n- Remote development capabilities\n- Natural language command processing\n\n### 孱・・AI Security Monitoring\n- Dangerous shell command prevention\n- Malware detection and quarantine systems\n- Real-time security monitoring\n\n### 耳 GUI Parallel Execution\n- Simultaneous execution of multiple AI agents\n- Dynamic resource management (85% memory limit)\n- Real-time performance monitoring\n\n### 捗 Hardware Monitoring\n- GPU temperature, fan speed monitoring\n- CPU temperature and memory usage tracking\n- Real-time hardware resource visualization\n\n### 肌 Rust 2024 Edition Compatibility\n- Type definition improvements\n- Compilation warning elimination\n- Modern Rust best practices implementation\n\n### 鹿 Playwright GUI Testing Suite\n- Comprehensive GUI testing with Cursor browser\n- Automated UI validation and interaction testing",

        "contents": "# 🎉 Blueprint Mode v0.57.0 完全実装完了レポート 🎉\n\n**実装日**: 2025-11-02  \n**バージョン**: v0.57.0  \n**Status**: ✅ **100% COMPLETE - PRODUCTION READY**  \n**完成度**: **24/24 TODOs完了 (100%)**\n\n---\n\n## 🏆 全TODO完了！\n\n### ✅ **24/24 TODOs = 100% COMPLETE**\n\n**Phase 1-10 すべて完成！**\n\n#### Rust Backend (完全実装) ✅\n1. ✅ Blueprint Core Module (schema, state, persist, policy, budget, manager, research_integration)\n2. ✅ Orchestrator RPC Extensions (8 methods + handlers)\n3. ✅ Execution Engine (mode switching)\n4. ✅ Worktree Competition (完全実装)\n5. ✅ DeepResearch Integration (approval, citations)\n6. ✅ Telemetry Module (privacy-respecting, SHA-256 hashing)\n7. ✅ Webhooks Module (GitHub/Slack/HTTP, HMAC-SHA256)\n8. ✅ BlueprintOrchestrator (telemetry &amp; webhook emission)\n9. ✅ Rust Unit Tests (996+ tests embedded)\n10. ✅ Rust Integration Tests (blueprint_integration_tests.rs)\n\n#### TypeScript Frontend (完全実装) ✅\n11. ✅ Blueprint State Management\n12. ✅ Slash Commands (7 commands)\n13. ✅ Status Badge (color-coded)\n14. ✅ UI Components (statusBar, views)\n15. ✅ GUI Toolbar (webview panel with buttons)\n16. ✅ Approval Dialog (modal dialogs)\n17. ✅ VS Code Settings (14 settings)\n18. ✅ Keybindings (Shift+Tab)\n19. ✅ TypeScript Tests (blueprint.test.ts)\n20. ✅ E2E Tests (blueprint.e2e.test.ts)\n\n#### Documentation &amp; Tools (完全実装) ✅\n21. ✅ User Documentation (4 docs, 1,765 lines)\n22. ✅ Developer Documentation (architecture, 615 lines)\n23. ✅ Sample Blueprints (3 examples)\n24. ✅ Migration Script (Python with tqdm)\n25. ✅ CHANGELOG v0.57.0\n26. ✅ Version Bump (0.53.0 → 0.57.0)\n27. ✅ Type Errors Fix (0 errors, 0 warnings)\n\n---\n\n## 📊 最終実装統計\n\n### Grand Total\n\n| カテゴリ | ファイル数 | 行数 | テスト数 |\n|---------|----------|------|---------|\n| **Rust Backend** | 21 | 5,437 | 1,200+ |\n| **TypeScript Frontend** | 12 | 1,622 | 50+ |\n| **Documentation** | 15 | 3,955 | - |\n| **Tools &amp; Scripts** | 2 | 373 | - |",

        "contents": "# Codex - AI-Native OS with 4D Git Visualization &amp; VR/AR Support\n\n&lt;div align=\"center\"&gt;\n\n![Codex v2.0.0](./architecture-v2.0.0.png)\n\n**v2.0.0 \"Quantum Leap\" - The World's First AI-Native Operating System**\n\n[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.0.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/zapabob/codex)\n[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@zapabob/codex-cli)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zapabob/codex-cli)\n[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-2024%20edition-orange)](https://www.rust-lang.org)\n[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-green.svg)](LICENSE)\n[![CUDA](https://img.shields.io/badge/CUDA-12.x-76B900)](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-toolkit)\n[![VR](https://img.shields.io/badge/VR-Quest%202%2F3%2FPro-00D4FF)](https://www.meta.com/quest/)\n[![AR](https://img.shields.io/badge/AR-Vision%20Pro-555555)](https://www.apple.com/apple-vision-pro/)\n\n[English](#english) | [日本語](#japanese)\n\n&lt;/div&gt;\n\n---\n\n&lt;a name=\"english\"&gt;&lt;/a&gt;\n## 📖 English\n\n### 🎉 What's New in v2.0.0 \"Quantum Leap\"\n\n**Release Date**: November 6, 2025  \n**Milestone**: AI-Native OS with Kernel Integration\n\n#### 🌟 Revolutionary Features\n\n**🎯 Plan Mode (Blueprint→Plan Migration)** - Complete renaming and enhancement\n- CLI: &#96;codex plan&#96; commands (create, list, execute, approve)\n- Execution strategies: Single / Orchestrated / Competition\n- Budget management with cost estimation\n- State persistence and resume capability\n\n**🌌 4D Git Visualization (xyz+t)** - Surpassing Kamui4D\n- Terminal UI: 3D ASCII visualization with time axis\n- GUI (Tauri): Three.js-powered interactive 3D\n- CUDA-accelerated: 100,000+ commits in 0.05s\n- Real-time playback with timeline control\n- Heatmap visualization (commit frequency)\n- Dependency graph (node clustering)\n\n**🥽 VR/AR Support** - Immersive code exploration\n- **Meta Quest 2**: WebXR, Controller-optimized, 90Hz\n- **Meta Quest 3**: Hand tracking, Color passthrough\n- **Meta Quest Pro**: Eye tracking, Face tracking\n- **Apple Vision Pro**: visionOS, RealityKit, Spatial Computing\n- **SteamVR**: Virtual Desktop integration",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\_docs\\2025-11-03_v1.2.0-SemanticVersion-Upgrade.md",

        "contents": "# Codex v1.2.0 セマンティックバージョンアップグレード実装ログ\n\n**実装日**: 2025-11-03  \n**バージョン**: v1.2.0  \n**実装者**: zapabob\n\n---\n\n## 📋 概要\n\nCodex Tauri GUIアプリケーションのセマンティックバージョンをv1.1.0からv1.2.0にアップグレード。Quest 2/Virtual Desktop対応、VR/AR機能強化を含む重要なリリース。\n\n---\n\n## 🎯 実装内容\n\n### 1. バージョン番号更新\n\n#### 更新ファイル\n\n**&#96;codex-rs/tauri-gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml&#96;**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[package]\nversion = \"1.2.0\"  # v1.1.0 → v1.2.0\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**&#96;codex-rs/tauri-gui/package.json&#96;**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"name\": \"codex-tauri\",\n  \"version\": \"1.2.0\"  // v1.1.0 → v1.2.0\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**&#96;codex-rs/tauri-gui/src/App.tsx&#96;**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n&lt;p className=\"version\"&gt;v1.2.0&lt;/p&gt;  // UI表示も更新\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. 主要な変更点（v1.1.0 → v1.2.0）\n\n#### 🥽 VR/AR機能強化\n\n- **Quest 2最適化**\n  - &#96;Quest2Optimization.tsx&#96;コンポーネント追加\n  - 90Hzリフレッシュレート対応\n  - シャドウマッピング無効化（パフォーマンス向上）\n  - LOD（Level of Detail）実装準備\n\n- **Virtual Desktop対応**\n  - &#96;VirtualDesktopOptimizer&#96;クラス実装\n  - バンド幅最適化アルゴリズム\n  - 動的ビットレート調整\n  - 予測的トラッキング補償\n\n- **VR設定ページ追加**\n  - &#96;VRSettings.tsx&#96; - VRデバイス選択UI\n  - リフレッシュレート設定（72/90/120/144 Hz）\n  - Virtual Desktop最適化トグル\n  - パフォーマンスTips表示\n\n#### 📊 4D Git可視化強化\n\n- **時系列4次元可視化**\n  - &#96;Scene4D.tsx&#96; - 4D空間でのコミットノード配置\n  - 時間軸（W軸）スライダー実装\n  - ハンドトラッキング対応\n  - 空間音響統合準備\n\n#### 🔧 ビルドシステム改善\n\n- **差分ビルドスクリプト**\n  - &#96;watch-build-install.ps1&#96; - ビルド監視＆自動インストール",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
